parts.label: whole
parts.display_text: A charged particle moves at 1.1 × 10⁶ m s⁻¹ perpendicular to a magnetic field of 0.052 T. An electric field is added so that the particle continues with constant velocity. Calculate the required electric field strength.

answer.text: The electric and magnetic forces must be equal and opposite: |q|E = |q|vB. E = vB = 5.7 × 10⁴ N C⁻¹.

parts.label: whole
parts.display_text: A loose metal helical spring rests on a smooth table with equally spaced turns. Flexible leads connect its ends to a dc supply. Describe and explain how the spacing between turns changes when current starts flowing.

answer.text: The spacing decreases. Adjacent turns carry current in the same sense. Each turn’s magnetic field acts on the current in neighbouring turns, producing attraction.

parts.label: whole
parts.display_text: Particle 1 has charge −Q and particle 2 has charge +2Q. Each starts from rest and is accelerated through a potential difference of the same magnitude ΔV, with polarity chosen to accelerate that particle. Determine K2/K1.

answer.text: The kinetic energy gained is |q|ΔV. Thus K1 = QΔV, K2 = 2QΔV and K2/K1 = 2.

parts.label: whole
parts.display_text: A particle of mass M/2 and positive charge 2Q enters a uniform field B0 perpendicular to the field at speed v = 2√(K2/M), where K2 is its kinetic energy. It completes a semicircle before leaving the field. Derive its entry-to-exit separation in terms of M, Q, K2 and B0.

answer.text: The radius is r = mv/(qB0) = [(M/2) × 2√(K2/M)]/(2QB0) = √(MK2)/(2QB0). Entry and exit are separated by a diameter: Δx = √(MK2)/(QB0).

parts.label: whole
parts.display_text: A negatively charged particle moves vertically down the page through a magnetic field directed out of the page. An electric field is added so that its path is straight and its speed constant. Determine the direction of the electric field.

answer.text: The magnetic force on the negative charge is to the right. Its electric force must be to the left, so the electric field points to the right.

parts.label: whole
parts.display_text: A circular wire loop lies in the page. Its left half is inside a uniform field directed into the page; its right half is outside the field. An anticlockwise current flows around the loop. State and explain the direction of the resultant magnetic force on the loop.

answer.text: The resultant is to the right. On the left-hand semicircle the current is directed from the top towards the bottom. Applying the current–field force rule to small sections gives rightward components that add; upward and downward components cancel by symmetry. The right half experiences no magnetic force.

parts.label: whole
parts.display_text: An electron starts from rest in a uniform electric field of magnitude 1.41 × 10⁶ N C⁻¹. Its mass is 9.11 × 10⁻³¹ kg and charge is −1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C. Find its initial acceleration, including its direction relative to the field.

answer.text: The force magnitude is eE = (1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹)(1.41 × 10⁶) = 2.26 × 10⁻¹³ N. Initial acceleration a = eE/m = 2.48 × 10¹⁷ m s⁻², opposite to the field.

parts.label: whole
parts.display_text:
Positive ions travel horizontally to the right through crossed uniform electric and magnetic fields. The upper plate is positive and the lower plate negative. Plate separation is d and potential difference is V; use E = V/d.

(a) Derive the speed u for an ion to pass undeviated.
(b) For speed 1.60 × 10⁵ m s⁻¹, V = 980 V and d = 3.6 × 10⁻² m, determine B.
(c) Explain whether an alpha particle at the same selected speed also passes undeviated.
(d) Determine the direction of B.
(e) If a positive ion enters faster, give its initial deflection direction and explain why.

answer.text:
(a) Electric and magnetic forces oppose and balance: qE = quB, giving u = E/B = V/(Bd).
(b) B = 980/[(3.6 × 10⁻²)(1.60 × 10⁵)] = 0.170 T.
(c) Yes. The selected speed does not depend on mass or charge; both forces scale with q.
(d) Electric force is downward, so magnetic force must be upward. For positive ions moving right, B is into the page.
(e) At entry, qvB exceeds qE, so the initial resultant and curvature are upward.

parts.label: whole
parts.display_text: An electromagnet’s uniform magnetic field B is proportional to current I. At current +0.5I₁, a moving charged particle feels magnetic force F_B leftward. What current makes the force 2F_B rightward? Explain.

answer.text: Use current −I₁. Doubling current magnitude from 0.5I₁ to I₁ doubles B and therefore doubles |qvB|. Reversing current reverses B, which reverses the magnetic-force direction.

parts.label: whole
parts.display_text: A proton enters a 0.030 T magnetic field into the page at 3.0×10⁵ m s⁻¹, moving right. Find the magnetic force, sketch its path and compare a faster proton’s path. Then find the electric field that makes the first proton undeflected.

answer.text: F=qvB=(1.60×10⁻¹⁹)(3.0×10⁵)(0.030)=1.44×10⁻¹⁵ N, upward by the right-hand rule. It follows an upward circular arc; the faster proton has larger radius r=mv/(qB). For no deflection, qE balances the upward magnetic force, so E=vB=9.0×10³ N C⁻¹ downward.

answer.text: A. Apply F=IL×B or Fleming’s left-hand rule to the indicated current and N-to-S field: the force is out of the page.

parts.label: whole
parts.display_text: A particle of mass m and charge magnitude |q| is accelerated from rest through potential difference V by the electric field. (a) Show v=√(2|q|V/m) and state the principle. (b) Find electron speed after 200 V.

answer.text: Official report checked; editorial worked explanation: conservation of energy gives |q|V=½mv² and v=√(2|q|V/m). For an electron, v=√[2(1.602×10⁻¹⁹)(200)/(9.11×10⁻³¹)]=8.39×10⁶ m s⁻¹.

evidence.detail: Official VCAA 2022 NHT report checked for Section B Question 1; explanation is editorial.

parts.label: whole
parts.display_text: A positron enters from the left and an electron enters from the right at equal speed into the uniform magnetic field shown by crosses. Their masses are equal and their charges have equal magnitude but opposite sign. Draw and label the path of each particle.

answer.text: Official report checked; editorial worked explanation: both bend upward in equal-radius circular arcs. With B into the page, q(v×B) is upward for each because both q and v reverse; equal mass, speed and |q| give equal radii.
